requirements.statement: When the path is expressed using bracket notation (e.g., "[key]") and the target is an array, a plain object, a primitive value, or null/undefined, lodash.set returns the target (or a new object) after setting the value.

When the path is expressed using dot notation (e.g., "a.b") and the target is an array, a plain object, a primitive value, or null/undefined, lodash.set returns the target (or a new object) after setting the value.
When the path is empty (i.e., no path segments) and the target is an array, a plain object, a primitive value, or null/undefined, lodash.set returns the target unchanged.
When the path contains a mixture of dot and bracket notation, lodash.set returns the target after setting the value for array, plain object, or primitive targets, and also for null/undefined targets.

When the path attempts prototype pollution (e.g., "__proto__" or "constructor.prototype"), lodash.set may either return the target, throw a TypeError, or perform prototype pollution depending on the target type.
When using dot notation on an array target, lodash.set may throw a non‑TypeError exception in rare cases.
When using mixed notation on a plain object target, lodash.set may throw a non‑TypeError exception in rare cases.
